scenes.narration: About half the nitrogen atoms in your body passed through a factory reactor.
scenes.title: HALF OF YOU IS SYNTHETIC

scenes.narration: Air is 78 percent nitrogen, but a triple bond locks it away.
In 1909, Fritz Haber made ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen in the lab. Carl Bosch scaled it up, and the first plant opened in 1913.
Hydrogen from natural gas meets nitrogen from air over a hot iron catalyst. The reactor runs at 400 to 500 degrees Celsius and around 200 bar.
scenes.caption: 400–500 °C · ~200 BAR

scenes.narration: Each pass converts 15 percent, but recycling lifts the total to 97 percent.
Ammonia plants use roughly 1 to 2 percent of all the world's energy.
scenes.sub: of world energy goes into ammonia

scenes.narration: The fertilizer that results feeds about 48 percent of all humanity.
Since 1900, world population has grown from 1.6 billion to 8 billion.
Strictly, that half is a popular estimate, not a precisely measured value.
scenes.caption: AN ESTIMATE
scenes.sub: the 48% counts people fed, not body nitrogen

scenes.narration: You are partly made of air, pressed into shape by iron. Follow for more.

sources.claim: Popular claim: about half the nitrogen in a human body has passed through Haber-Bosch (Hager, The Alchemy of Air). Popular-science estimate, not a measured value.
Popular claim: about half the nitrogen in a human body has passed through Haber-Bosch (Hager, The Alchemy of Air). Popular-science estimate, not a measured value.
Same claim as phrased by Tom Standage: about half the nitrogen atoms in your body have passed through a Haber-Bosch reaction.
Air is over 78% nitrogen but gaseous N2 is chemically and biologically unusable; fertilizer from ammonia supports almost half the world population (Erisman et al. 2008, Nature Geoscience).
N2 is bound by a triple bond, which makes it relatively inert.
Haber synthesised ammonia in 1909; BASF gave scale-up to Carl Bosch; first ammonia synthesis plant went into operation at Oppau in 1913.
Haber synthesised ammonia in 1909; BASF gave scale-up to Carl Bosch; first ammonia synthesis plant went into operation at Oppau in 1913.
Commercial plants: multi-promoted iron catalyst, 400-500 C, pressures above 100 bar; most plants operate in roughly 130-220 bar (spoken as 'around 200 bar'; brief range 150-300 bar).

Hydrogen comes from natural gas by steam methane reforming (IEA: ~77% of ammonia is gas-based).

About 15% conversion per pass; unreacted gas is recycled; overall conversion ~97% (some texts say ~98%).
